author: potuz
content:
I want to point here my take on the issue of lowering the retention period cause it may seem that I'm just fighting just to pick up a fight. There are two topics about changing the block retention period. One is to align the EL and the CL, the other is to lower it.  We were stupid enough to lock unnecessarily EL and CL syncing so the spec requires us to keep at least the number of blocks that is needed to sync and obey the spec. So I think there is no contention about the first part: we should and must align the CL and EL on the number of blocks that are needed (or force layers to keep twice the same data to make sure). 

What I don't like is that this comes with an automatic reduction. 8061 is a piece of the puzzle, but it is not all of it. There are different reasons why blocks are retained on either layer and the right number of blocks that we may want nodes to be forced to have may be different on either layer. Unfortunately again we are forced to be aligned so we may be forced to keep more blocks than strictly needed. On the CL side we only need whatever the WSP dictates. But that's to sync, this says nothing about history, or RPC servers finding peers to get past blocks, etc... So even if we were to align on both layers, it's not clear at all to me that we want to reduce on both sides. I, as a CL dev, can only vouch that we don't need more than what the WSP requires. But I'm pretty sure the people that care about CROPS may want to force most nodes to keep a longer window of history available in a trustless and decentralized manner.
